Synopsis:
    Petrobras is preparing a ~1 BRL/liter diesel price hike at its refineries, pending Brazilian government subsidy measures to offset consumer impact. The move is driven by a widening gap between domestic and international diesel prices, itself a result of Middle East conflict and Russian export restrictions. A new 1 BRL/liter subsidy would be layered on top of an existing ~1.12 BRL/liter subsidy to cushion end-users. Brazil imports ~25% of its diesel needs, creating margin pressure on Petrobras when international prices exceed domestic ones.
